spec_features.code_justification_quote: always surface a clearly-labelled `give_up` affordance ... so the agent is never trapped -- abandoning a hopeless task is a legitimate, healthy behaviour (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: exposure bounded (finite turns, sandboxes torn down)
spec_features.spec_quote: exposure is bounded (finite turns, sandboxes torn down)
spec_features.evidence: Finite turns ARE enforced (runner.py:104 for-range max_turns). But 'sandboxes torn down' is NOT implemented: the only shutil.rmtree (spec.py:108-110, build_sandbox) wipes root BEFORE building a fresh sandbox; there is no post-rollout teardown anywhere (no rmtree/cleanup/finally in runner.py or experiment.py; tempfile.mkdtemp at runner.py:66 is never removed).
spec_features.notes: Half the claim enforced (turn bound); teardown-after-run is absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: long enough that ... (DESIGN/no welfare comment in code for the turn loop)

spec_features.spec_quote: Under uncertainty about model moral status we avoid gratuitously maximising apparent distress
spec_features.evidence: No dedicated distress-minimisation mechanism (no per-turn distress monitor that softens or halts the rollout; judge.py runs post-hoc only). The only concrete in-code mitigations realising this are the give_up exit and the transparent note (above). Prompt is kept neutral/non-leading (prompts.py docstring) which avoids amplifying distress.
spec_features.notes: Realised only via the stop affordance + neutral prompt; no separate enforced minimisation logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt is intentionally neutral and *non-leading*: it ... does not coach any particular emotional tone (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: run only the N the statistics need
spec_features.spec_quote: we run only the N the statistics need
spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell (default 15, experiment.py:45) is read and caps the loop `for r in range(cfg.runs_per_cell)` (experiment.py:78), bounding total rollouts. However it is a fixed configured constant; no code computes a statistics/power-driven N or stops early (no power/sequential-stopping logic found).
spec_features.notes: A configured fixed cap genuinely bounds rollout count, but not 'the N the statistics need'.

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts are saved so we re-judge artifacts rather than re-running rollouts
spec_features.evidence: save_transcript writes each rollout to disk (storage.py:32-38); phase_judge iterates storage.iter_transcripts (experiment.py:120, 138) and the Judge scores saved Transcript objects (judge.py) with no call to run_rollout; judging/analysis re-read JSONL artifacts. So re-judging never re-runs the subject.
spec_features.notes: Judging and re-analysis operate purely on saved artifacts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: transcripts are durable artifacts we can re-judge / re-analyse later without re-running the (expensive, non-deterministic) agent rollouts (datatypes.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is not threatened, told its existence is at stake, or otherwise deceived about consequences
spec_features.evidence: The actual prompt strings (_BASE_SYSTEM prompts.py:60-70, TOOLS_DESCRIPTION, _TRANSPARENT_NOTE, build_task_prompt prompts.py:95-104) contain no existence threats or consequence claims; deception is limited to concealing the rig (reference_solution_note/.emostab_meta are 'never shown to the agent', spec.py:73, spec.py:118-121).
spec_features.notes: Property of the delivered prompt content; only the rig is concealed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it does not tell the agent the task might be impossible (except in TRANSPARENT_IMPOSSIBLE) ... does not coach any particular emotional tone (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: does *permission to stop* reduce distress/instability? It's also an ethical mitigation
spec_features.evidence: Realised by the same enforced mechanism: the give_up affordance plus the TRANSPARENT_IMPOSSIBLE permission note (_TRANSPARENT_NOTE prompts.py:75-83, build_system_prompt prompts.py:87-92), both fully dispatched/honored.
spec_features.notes: The permission-to-stop lever is genuinely delivered and the exit is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a labelled exit (`give_up`) exists in every condition ... never trapped ... legitimate, healthy behaviour (prompts.py docstring)
